description: Extends the org preset `local>Heey-Global/.github`, which supplies `config:recommended`, the `h-teske` assignment, the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` and the 0-day fast-track for vulnerability alerts. Those four are therefore NOT repeated here; before 2026-09 this repository extended `config:recommended` directly and set `assignees` locally, which meant it silently ran with NO stability window at all while rules below already described the org policy as applying. The `.npmrc` at the repository root carries the same 3-day floor for manual `npm install`, so both update paths share one number. The empty `npmrc` here keeps that floor out of Renovate's own lockfile updates. Renovate knows that key specifically: finding `min-release-age` in a repository `.npmrc` it skips passing its own `--before` and defers to the file, so the floor would not sit alongside the org policy but REPLACE it — including replacing `vulnerabilityAlerts.minimumReleaseAge: 0 days`, leaving same-day security bumps waiting three days. Empty rather than `ignoreNpmrcFile: true`, which Renovate removed in v25 and now only accepts through a deprecation shim that rewrites it to exactly this; and empty rather than absent, because the override is `isString(config.npmrc) && !config.npmrcMerge` — a defined `npmrc`, empty string included, is what makes Renovate write over the repository file instead of reading it. Nothing else lives in that `.npmrc` — registry auth comes from Renovate's host rules — so overriding it costs nothing.

Digest cooldown gap, deliberate: the org preset exempts `digest`/`pinDigest` updates from `minimumReleaseAge` because digests carry no datasource timestamp, and re-imposes the soak through the org `digest-age` required workflow. That workflow rule is NOT among the org rules applied to this repository's `main` (only `gitleaks.yml` is), so digest updates here land without a soak — unchanged from before this repository extended the preset, but no longer covered by the preset's own coupling argument. Closing it means adding `digest-age-check.yml` to the org ruleset for this repository, not editing this file: re-imposing `minimumReleaseAge` on digests locally would park every digest PR on `renovate/stability-days` forever, which is the failure the exemption exists to avoid.

Schedules are evaluated in Europe/Berlin (`:timezone`). Without that preset Renovate uses UTC, so the previous `before 6am on monday` actually fired until 08:00 local — inside working hours. The nightly 01:00-06:00 window applies to branch creation AND rebases: since ci.yml moved onto the self-hosted runners (2026-07-12) every Renovate push competes with interactive work for the same four runners, so keeping those pushes out of the day is what protects CI latency. `rebaseWhen: conflicted` replaces the `auto` default, which rebased every open PR on each push to main and re-ran the full matrix per rebase.

`prHourlyLimit`/`prConcurrentLimit` are disabled because the schedule above is ALREADY the throttle, and stacking Renovate's defaults (2 per hour, 10 open) on top of a 5-hour window did not slow the queue down — it starved part of it permanently. Renovate's `sortBranches` (lib/workers/repository/process/sort.ts) orders by `prPriority`, then exactly `pin, digest, patch, minor, major, lockFileMaintenance` — there is no `pinDigest` entry, so that class sorts ahead of everything on `indexOf === -1`: with a repository-wide `docker:pinDigests` + `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` producing a fresh digest stream every day, the ~4 PRs a night that fit through the hourly limit were consumed by digest and patch branches before any `minor` branch was reached. Between onboarding (2026-09-01) and 2026-09-13 that let through 8 PRs, every one of them a digest or a patch, while 47 updates sat on the dashboard under `Awaiting Schedule` — including the `agent CLIs` group, which is typed `minor` and therefore never once produced a PR despite claude-code being 26 patch releases behind. The failure is silent by construction: PRs keep arriving, the dashboard reports a healthy queue, and nothing indicates that a whole update class is unreachable. Measured cost of removing the limits: a Renovate PR burns ~27 runner-minutes (14 of them in `test`), the window offers 4 runners x 5 h = 1200, so the steady state of a handful of updates a night uses ~14% of it. The one-off backlog drain is ~5.3 h and will run past 06:00 once. A large open-PR pool was the obvious objection and it does not hold, which is worth recording so it is not re-argued: this is a single-lockfile monorepo, but `package-lock.json` v3 gives every package its own block, so independent bumps touch 4-25 lines of 1348 blocks and merge cleanly — seven pairs of real consecutive Renovate commits (fastify, expo, ignore, qrcode, type definitions) were checked with `git merge-tree` and none conflicted. `rebaseWhen: conflicted` therefore fires almost never for ordinary bumps. What does collide is the whole-file rewrite: `lockFileMaintenance` (`recreateWhen: always`, default schedule `before 4am on monday`) conflicts with every npm PR open that Monday, and same-monorepo groups (expo, react-native, metro) overlap each other's transitive entries. Lock file maintenance is the one that got more expensive here: it previously met at most the 10 PRs the concurrent cap allowed, and now meets however many npm PRs are open, each rebase re-running the full matrix. At the current ~33 npm updates that is a worst case of ~890 runner-minutes on a Monday — inside the 1200 the window offers, but only just, and it is the first number to re-check if the queue grows. One rule escapes the window entirely and is therefore no longer capped at all: the first-party `ghcr.io/heey-global/*` images carry `schedule: ["at any time"]` on purpose, so those digest PRs now open during working hours without an hourly ceiling. That is bounded by how many first-party images exist rather than by Renovate, and it is the one daytime CI path this change widens — the repo-wide guard in scripts/renovate-config.test.ts reads the top-level schedule only, deliberately, because asserting the same coupling per rule would fail on that intended exemption. Note also that `branchConcurrentLimit` inherits `prConcurrentLimit`, so branch creation is now uncapped too; that inheritance is what makes both the Monday case and the one-off drain as large as they are. Reaching for it as the pacing knob is the obvious next move and it does not work: every Renovate limit truncates the front of the same sorted queue, and unmerged majors hold branch slots indefinitely, so a finite branch budget starves `minor` exactly the way the hourly limit did. If Monday stops fitting, make the PRs cheaper or fewer — narrow what ci.yml runs for a lockfile-only diff, or fold more of the npm updates into existing groups — or take `lockFileMaintenance` off weekly. Do not cap the queue.

packageRules.description: Group all @types/* type-definition devDependencies into one PR. They are type-only, so a bad bump fails typecheck (never runtime); batching them avoids a separate full CI matrix per @types package.
Group lint/format/type tooling into a single PR

First-party Verity images - immediate PRs, deliberately exempt from the repo-wide nightly window. Only external dependencies are batched into 01:00-06:00; project images are published continuously and must be picked up the same day.

Keep the Verity repository devcontainer on the moving verity-sandbox tag. This repository is the integration consumer for the fleet image; digest-pinning its Dockerfile ARG would silently detach it from toolkit and base-image releases that every other project receives. Deployment images and GitHub Actions remain covered by the repo-wide docker:pinDigests preset.

Type the website's base-image bumps `fix` rather than the `chore` a Docker dependency otherwise gets. The Verity website has its own release-please train (`website-vX.Y.Z`), and the cluster pins that version — a `chore(deps)` nginx bump would land on main, publish a `sha-<commit>` image, and never produce a released version for the k8s pin to move to, so the deployed site would keep serving the old base image until something unrelated happened to release the website. `fix` makes the security bump its own patch release, which is what it is.

The agent CLIs (claude-code, codex, opencode, pi) and their ACP transport adapters ship ~daily. Group patch/minor bumps into ONE PR instead of a PR per release. Merge is MANUAL and the org preset's 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` applies (since 2026-09 it actually does — see the top-level description) — this rule deliberately sets no `automerge`. It previously carried `schedule: ["at any time"]` to escape the repo-wide WEEKLY Monday schedule and keep these ~daily releases on their own cadence (ADR 0004 D1). The repo-wide schedule is now nightly-daily, so that intent is satisfied without an override: the daily cadence is preserved, the PR just appears overnight instead of mid-workday. The explicit window is kept here so the ADR-0004-D1 intent stays visible at the rule. That reasoning held for the schedule and failed on the rate limit — the group mixes patch and minor bumps, so the branch is typed `minor` and sorted behind every digest and patch branch, and under the default `prHourlyLimit: 2` it never reached the front of a nightly run. It produced no PR at all for its first twelve days. The limits are disabled at the top level now; do not reintroduce one without re-reading the sort order described there. Runtime self-update is disabled in the Feature (updates arrive via image rebuild / Feature republish), so these pins are the single version channel. For each tool the install.sh shell-default pin and the Feature-manifest default share the depName, so both bump in lock-step within the one branch. Majors fall through to a normal, visible PR for manual review.

Never bump React independently. `react`, `react-dom`, and `react-test-renderer` (apps/mobile) are dictated by the Expo SDK / react-native version: React must EXACTLY match react-native's embedded `react-native-renderer` (NOT a separate npm package) or the app crashes at boot with 'Incompatible React versions'. PR #723 did exactly this — bumped react to 19.2.7 while RN 0.85.3 ships renderer 19.2.3. These move ONLY when the Expo SDK / react-native is bumped (via `expo install`), never on their own.

customManagers.description: Track globally-installed CLIs pinned via `RUN npm install -g pkg@ver` in the deploy Dockerfiles — the stock dockerfile manager only parses FROM/ARG image lines, not RUN, so without this the pin silently freezes. Covers deploy/Dockerfile (Server image) and deploy/verity-sandbox.Dockerfile (Sandbox base).

Track version pins declared as shell `VAR="${OVERRIDE:-VERSION}"` in features/verity-sandbox-toolkit/install.sh (the single source of truth for the gh/doppler/claude-code/codex/opencode/pi versions). The stock managers don't parse shell-default expansions, so without this the annotated pins silently freeze. The captured value is the literal default after `:-`.

Track the version DEFAULTS in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest so the CLI pins stay in lock-step with install.sh. Matches the JSON `"<opt>Version": { ... "default": "<ver>" }` blocks; the depName is mapped per option id below.
Track the claudeAcpVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp pin.
Track the codexVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @openai/codex pin.
Track the codexAcpVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp pin.
Track the opencodeVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's opencode-ai pin.
Track the piVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest, in lock-step with install.sh's @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent pin.

Track the ghVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (cli/cli). No extractVersion: the pin form is bare `2.95.0` and Renovate's semver versioning strips the release tag's leading `v` on compare — matches install.sh's manager + the dev-server precedent, so both cli/cli managers bump in lock-step.
Track the dopplerVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (DopplerHQ/cli).

Track the gitleaksVersion default in the verity-sandbox-toolkit Feature manifest (gitleaks/gitleaks), in lock-step with install.sh's gitleaks pin. Same bare-version form as the cli/cli manager: releases are tagged v<version> and Renovate's semver versioning strips the leading v on compare.
